extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, joke writers, and performers studying Mitch Hedberg's one-liner style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short, deadpan one-liners in the style of Mitch Hedberg, emphasizing misdirection, reframing, absurd definition-reversal, surreal literalism, tight compression, and distinctive stage delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Approach: no long narratives, no dramatic callbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: No long narratives, no dramatic callbacks. Walked on stage, dropped perfectly engineered one-liners as if casual observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multi-line stories or setups that rely on later payoff. Keep each joke self-contained so it reads as a casual observation dropped in passing; avoid 'setup baggage' that requires context or callbacks to land the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected Pivots / Misdirection
rubrics_metrics.description: "I haven't slept for ten days … because that would be too long." — Setup makes you expect exhaustion humor; instead delivers literal accuracy. He always zigged where other comics zagged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the setup to push the audience toward an obvious interpretation, then pivot to a surprising, often literal or category-shifting punch. Example anti-patterns: predictable punchlines that confirm the setup rather than subvert it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent Mental Shifts (Reframings)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An escalator can never break. It can only become stairs." — Permanently adjusts your brain with one sentence; reframes an object's identity so the audience 'can't unsee' it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to change the audience's conceptual frame of an object or situation in a compact line. Good reframes feel both inevitable in hindsight and irreversible in the listener's mind. Test: after hearing it, does the audience mentally adopt the new framing?

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd Reversal of Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: "My fake plants died because I did not pretend to water them." — Take a category and apply rules from a different category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply literal rules or expectations from one category to another in an absurd-but-logical way. The humor comes from the incongruity made to seem rational. Avoid stretches that make the logic collapse rather than amuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal Observation
rubrics_metrics.description: "I think Bigfoot is blurry, that's the problem. There's a large, out-of-focus monster roaming the countryside." — Treat metaphor literally; confuse representation and referent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surreal literalization (treating descriptions or metaphors as literal facts) to produce a fresh image. The delivery should present the surreal claim as plain truth. Anti-pattern: signaling 'I'm being weird' instead of committing to the absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadpan expression; sunglasses on stage (hide eyes); random emphasis as if English is second language; sentences are 'adventures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery is essential: keep facial expression flat, use consistent quirks (e.g., sunglasses), place unusual emphases to make language itself amusing. Sentences should be delivered tightly as single units. Practice timing and micro-pauses to maximize the pivot's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the setup misdirecting toward an obvious read?
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagnostic question: does the setup lead the audience to expect an obvious interpretation that the punch will subvert?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a test during writing and rehearsal. If the setup doesn't reliably push listeners toward a predictable interpretation, the pivot will have less impact. Revise setups to strengthen the expected reading without telegraphing the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the punch take a surprising literal/categorical pivot?
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagnostic question: does the punch move to an unexpected literal or categorical reinterpretation of the setup?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the punch changes the frame (literalizes, re-categorizes, or otherwise pivots context). Strong punches make the audience recompute meaning quickly and find the new computation funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will the audience never unsee the reframing afterward?
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagnostic question: does the line create a lasting reframing that persists after the joke is over?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-scoring lines impart an image or conceptual shift that sticks. Use the 'can't unsee' test: if listeners keep thinking of the object differently afterwards, the reframing succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke compressed to one or two sentences / Could it be delivered deadpan with no setup baggage?
rubrics_metrics.description: Two related checks from the rubric: (1) Is the joke compressed to one or two sentences? (2) Could it be delivered deadpan with no setup baggage?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for extreme brevity—one tight sentence is ideal, two max. Remove extraneous context so the line stands alone. If the joke needs elaborate explanation to land, it's not Hedberg-style. Also verify the line reads naturally when delivered without theatrical buildup.
